references.text: Rebekah's observation of Esau's plans in 27:5 leads directly to her rescue action in 27:42.
The motive for Esau's hunt in 27:5 is explained by Isaac's love for game meat in 25:28.
27:5 sets the hunt in motion while Rebekah listens; 27:30 marks Esau's return just after the deception.
Jacob's lie in 27:19 builds directly on Esau's mission from 27:5 to bring back game.
The time Esau spends hunting in 27:5 gives Rebekah time to fetch the clothes in 27:15.
Isaac's doubt in 27:21 arises because Jacob has taken Esau's place while he was out hunting (27:5).
The description of Esau as a man in the field in 25:27 explains his absence in 27:5.
Isaac's observation in 27:22 highlights the contrast between Jacob inside and Esau out hunting (27:5).
Esau's confirmation of identity in 27:32 occurs just as he arrives after the hunt that began in 27:5.
